texts.orig: Introduction: Several therapeutic options are usually discussed for otosclerosis management . Patients seek medical advice from an ENT specialist but This study intends to assess readability and quality of websites with information on otosclerosis Materials 63   Methods: This is a cross-sectionnal study performed in tertiary care center . The results of the first 2 pages of Google search with the keyword "otosclerosis" were reviewed by two independent investigators. Readability was assessed with the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL), Flesch   Reading Ease Score (FRES) and Gunning For quality and reliability assessment, the 16-items DISCERN instrument was used Inter-rater agreement was evaluated with concordance correlation coefficient . Results: 18 websites were included. Two websites (11.09) were authored by academic institutions; 5/18 (289) by government agencies; 6/18 (339) by professional organizations and 5/18 (289) The mean DISCERN 4 10.6, and the the mean FKGL was 11.4342.30 corresponding to "difficult to read" The mean Gunning index was 12.9042.19 (range 9.81- 18.20), corresponding to "college freshman" level. Conclusions: This study shows that internet information on otosclerosis has an overall low readability; while the quality is heterogeneous   and varies from "poor" to Efforts should be made to improve the readability of otosclerosis websites.
